trustSetup.title: Trust setup for Adobe Reader
trustSetup.subtitle: Install the local Certificate Authority so that Adobe shows the green checkmark on signed PDFs.
trustSetup.warningBody: This server runs a self-signed Certificate Authority for demonstration purposes. Import the CA certificate only on machines you control.
trustSetup.downloadDesc: Use the .cer file for Adobe Reader's import wizard. The PEM and CRL are provided for advanced/automation use.
trustSetup.adobeTitle: Import the CA into Adobe Reader
trustSetup.adobeDesc: Follow these steps once on each computer where you read signed PDFs:
trustSetup.adobeStep2: Go to Edit → Preferences → Signatures → Identities & Trusted Certificates → More.
trustSetup.adobeStep3: Open the Trusted Certificates tab and click Import.
trustSetup.adobeStep4: Browse to the downloaded .cer file and select it.
trustSetup.adobeStep5: Click Trust… and tick "Use this certificate as a trusted root" and "Certified documents → Signing".
trustSetup.adobeStep6: Click OK to confirm, then close the preferences dialog.
trustSetup.afterBody: Open any PDF you signed here. Adobe should display the green checkmark and "Signed and all signatures are valid". If you still see warnings, restart Acrobat Reader.
